city.caveat: This is the official city record as kept, without adjustments. It joins several observing sites over the years, and a move, a new instrument or the city growing around a station can shift readings (city growth mostly warms nights); NOAA's adjusted climate datasets correct for these. Treat any single number as approximate.

text.p_yest: The high of 79°F was typical for November 13. The normal high for the date is 76°F, and the record is 88°F (1934, 2021, 2025). The low of 58°F was the 14th warmest November 13 low (tied) of 132 since 1888.
text.t_rec: Record highs keep coming. Record lows have nearly stopped.
text.p_rec: If Needles' climate weren't changing, every year would have the same chance of holding a daily record. Since 2000, Needles has set 3 standing record lows, far fewer than the 74 that chance alone would give, and 171 record highs, far more than the 73 that chance alone would give. The 2020s hold the most record highs of any decade (76). Needles' all-time high is 125°F, on July 16, 1925.
text.t_chg: Needles' days and nights both warmed. Nights warmed faster.
text.p_chg: Across 109 complete years: Needles' average low has risen +0.47°F per decade (95% range +0.38 to +0.55), about +6.1°F since 1893. Needles' average high has risen +0.25°F per decade (95% range +0.16 to +0.33), about +3.3°F since 1893.
text.t_mon: Lows rose in all 12 months. Highs rose in 10 of 12 months.
text.p_rain: Needles' yearly precipitation shows no clear long-term change (−0.07 inches per decade, a range that includes zero). The 1991–2020 normal is 4.4 inches a year. The wettest year was 1939 (13.33 in); the driest, 1901 (0.50 in). Needles almost never sees snow (the 1991–2020 average is 0.0 inches a winter), so there's no snowfall chart.
